title: Enchiridion Syllabus
description: Schema for syllabus JSON files in syllabi/. A syllabus is an ordered, sectioned sequence of curricular items (texts, supplements, module chapters) representing a reading trajectory through the corpus. The canonical Grand Tour and any future preceptorials share this schema.

id.description: Stable identifier for the syllabus. Matches the filename (sans .json) and the URL slug (e.g., 'grand-tour', 'harmony-of-the-spheres').

kind.description: Distinguishes the canonical syllabus from thematic preceptorials. Canonical syllabi span the whole corpus chronologically; preceptorials are focused thematic trajectories.

description.description: One- or two-sentence summary of the syllabus's scope and intent.

sections.description: Ordered list of sections. For canonical syllabi these are typically the eight chronological eras; for preceptorials they are thematic chapters of the student's choosing.

id.description: Stable section identifier. For era sections this matches the directory name (e.g., '1-ancient-greece').

description.description: Optional short framing for the section. Longer framing essays should be supplements, not inline prose.

items.description: Ordered list of curricular items. Array order is the recommended reading sequence; concurrency and within-section flexibility are conveyed by visual treatment, not the schema.

type.description: What kind of item this is. Determines how the id is resolved.

id.description: Directory name for text/supplement items, or module directory name for module_chapter items (paired with the 'chapter' field).

chapter.description: Chapter identifier for module_chapter items. May be an integer index or the chapter filename stem (e.g., '03-the-case-system-and-the-article').

passages.description: Optional recommended passages within a text (e.g., ['Book I 1-32', 'Book V def. 1-7']). Curatorial recommendation, not a hard constraint. Free-form strings; rendering is the UI's responsibility.

note.description: Optional curatorial annotation specific to this item's role in the syllabus (e.g., 'read alongside the Greek module', 'capstone of the section'). Keep brief; substantive framing belongs in a supplement.
